# Contract delta 1 (binding; adopted 2026-09-26 by the coordinator after the synthesis cross-check)

Applies on top of synckit 6c3cec2, reposync f413e56, cc-sync f078f23, Orca a8da144. Each item names the lanes that implement it. Items the root review already rejected (silent rekey, printed second resume command, version whitelist, blanket LFS incompleteness, fixed size omissions, heuristic exclusions) stay rejected.

D1 RESOLVED by native fixtures (17135ee, 2026-09-26): after the adapter strips prompt_snapshot records (F6), a plain `claude --resume <id>` re-renders for the destination, and `--append-system-prompt <ctx>` IS honored (verified; --help advertises it). So D1 reduces to `recoveryLaunch?: Record<sourceProviderSessionId, {appendSystemPrompt: string (≤ 16 KiB)}>` carrying cc-sync's recovery context; `systemPromptSnapshot:'off'` is NOT needed and not added. Orca appends `--append-system-prompt <text>` (separate argv entry, never shell-parsed) for agent 'claude' only when the host claude's --help advertises it. Implemented in a post-QA Orca delta lane with its own tests. Original conditional text follows for history:
D1 (Orca import/resume; cc-sync sessionrestore/pickup/orcabridge) — conditional on native-fixtures findings: Orca import gains optional `recoveryLaunch?: Record<sourceProviderSessionId, {systemPromptSnapshot?: 'off'; appendSystemPrompt?: string (≤ 16 KiB)}>` (CLI `--recovery-launch-file <path>`), stored on the 'recovery' sleeping record; for agent 'claude' resume appends only the present fields as separate argv entries after host defaults (`--system-prompt-snapshot off`, `--append-system-prompt <text>`), never shell-parsed; this is the only allowlisted launch extension. cc-sync sends it only when the fixtures show the plain `claude --resume <id>` is insufficient after relocation AND the destination `claude --help` advertises the flag.

D2 (Orca import; cc-sync pickup/orcabridge; Orca picker): Orca import gains `sessionIdMap?: {from, to}[]` (CLI `--session-map from=to`, repeatable). Orca rewrites binding providerSession.id, the transcriptPath basename and structuredCursor.sessionId; `resume[]` takes LOCAL ids; result bindings report both source and local ids. cc-sync passes a mapping for every session forked with --on-divergence=fork (the only id-changing path).

D3 (cc-sync catalog/consumer): origin blocks are relayed VERBATIM, never filtered. A relayer includes a foreign origin block at revision r only when `store.Complete` holds for every non-expired checkpoint root in that block (artifact closure only; the relayer's own reposync Verify does not matter); otherwise it keeps exporting the last revision of that origin that met the bar. Equal revision with a different block digest → `origin-block-conflict` integrity error, no ACK. Every host applies ExpiresAt to foreign blocks locally. Local pickup readiness still requires Verify; ACK still requires every checkpoint in the change to be ready (closure + Verify); relay eligibility requires closure only.

D4 (synckit delivery-v2; cc-sync resident manifest): coalescing is a MAX-WAIT window in the deliverer: a (service, peer) worker made dirty at t runs at t+10 s for artifact services (immediately for v1 services); later kicks never extend the deadline. The cc-sync manifest uses `watch.debounce: "2s"`.

D5 (synckit artifact-store/syncservice-v2; cc-sync codesnap/capture): GCGrace = StagingTTL = 24 h. apply.v2 (progressive included) pins EVERY root in change.Artifacts under `synckit.accepted/<origin>`, complete or not; GC marking tolerates absent children. After a PartialError capture, cc-sync pins the refs already Put under `cc-sync/capture/<wtid>` until the next complete snapshot or 24 h. `codesnap.Has` = index hit AND store.Has.

D6 (cc-sync catalog/consumer): SourceRevision and every OriginBlock.Revision = max(prev + 1, now.UnixMicro()), persisted; they change only when the payload digest or root list changes. Per-origin fences are kept forever (compact).

D7 (cc-sync capture/catalog/cli; Orca picker): when code capture returns Deferred, Partial, MissingLFS, or a Complete=false snapshot, the job STILL archives the sessions and publishes a checkpoint whose code dependency is the most recent complete code manifest for that worktree (none if there is none), with `code_state: "deferred:<reason>"` + the named paths/objects and `code_captured_at`. An incomplete snapshot is never a root dependency. ErrBusy requeues in 30 s with no checkpoint. `cc-sync list` reports completeness.code 'deferred' plus `code_captured_at`, and the picker shows the code age distinctly from the session age (no false assurance).
  D7 CLARIFICATION (root review 2026-09-26, binding): such a MIXED checkpoint (newer session bytes + deferred/older code) is retained and delivered but is PARTIAL / NOT READY as a recovery point. Readiness for default pickup and for ACK assurance is defined over COMPLETE grouped checkpoints only (session bytes and code captured in the same round with code_state complete): the receiver's ACK of a change requires every complete checkpoint in it to be ready (closure + Verify); mixed checkpoints never make an ACK claim about themselves and never count as the worktree's recovery point. `cc-sync list`/picker show the latest COMPLETE checkpoint as the item's pick-up target, plus a visible "newer partial checkpoint (code deferred: <reason>, code age X, sessions age Y)" line; default pickup selects the previous complete grouped checkpoint. A mixed checkpoint is only restorable through an explicit `--checkpoint <id> --allow-partial` (JSON marks partial:true; never default, never auto-selected by the picker). Required test: after code capture becomes Deferred/Partial/MissingLFS, a new transcript turn produces a mixed checkpoint that is not ready, default pickup picks the earlier complete checkpoint, and the ACK readiness ignores the mixed one.

D8 (synckit delivery-v2/artifact-store/syncservice-v2): control traffic is only `synckit.net.status.v1` and `svc.capabilities`. Before every other peer call (have, closure, batch.*, apply.v2, pins.set), the sender re-runs Evaluate on its LIVE local state and a peer state no older than 2 min (re-probe otherwise). The receiver's `have` and apply.v2 handlers check the receiver's live state first and return the typed paused result before decoding the rest.

D9 (synckit artifact-store; cc-sync codesnap/capture/consumer): PutGroup with more than MaxDeps deps splits deterministically into a tree of `synckit.group` manifests. The closure bound applies PER ROOT; cc-sync checks each checkpoint closure at capture and never publishes a root over the bound (retain the last good one, name the cause). MaxRoots = 8192. Export overflow rule: include every worktree's latest checkpoint first, then hourly, then daily by recency until the cap; omitted ones are simply not exported (they remain retained locally and expire normally). Pin sets may hold up to 2 × MaxRoots during union-then-narrow.

D10 (synckit delivery-v2): TRANSFER checks the worker's dirty flag at every batch boundary; if set it returns ErrSuperseded, re-STAGEs with the CAS, and restarts TRANSFER in the new priority order (committed objects are kept), so a new human-tier checkpoint never waits behind a multi-GB backlog.

D11 (cc-sync consumer; reposync verify): ApplyArtifacts verifies with FetchOrigin=false; missing prerequisites record `prerequisites-missing` and return Partial. The resident runs the network-gated trunk fetch + Verify in the background (never inside the exclusive apply.v2 handler), then bumps the stamp so the next delivery ACKs.

D12 (cc-sync pickup/cli; Orca picker/import): (a) pickup passes `--register-repo` to `orca recovery import` (the checkout's repo is reposync-registered). (b) a live-local or divergent session that is NOT being resumed refuses only itself: per-session `status: 'refused'` + `reason` in pickup JSON (added to the picker's enum); a refused SELECTED resume session fails the pickup with its code. (c) pickup pins `cc-sync/pickup/<op>` expire after 24 h.

D13 (reposync + cc-sync scheduler; root requirement 2026-09-26T20:13Z): see cc-sync contract scheduler paragraph — `worktree.Stamp` code WIP stamp computed at due time gates Capture; configurable tier intervals/windows via config.json; E2E fixture for code-only edits.

D14 (reposync capture + stamp; coordinator 2026-09-26 after Stamp review f1f40ce): complete-WIP gaps in Capture that the Stamp review exposed. (a) Capture passes the worktree root PLUS every populated submodule root (recursive, from gitlinks) to vcs.FilterOverrideEnv so no clean/process filter configured only inside a submodule can run; core.fsmonitor=false is forced by ReadOnlyGitEnv/FilterOverrideEnv (landed in f1f40ce) for every source git read. (b) Paths marked assume-unchanged or skip-worktree (outside any active sparse-checkout pattern) whose working-tree bytes differ from the index are WIP that git status hides: Capture enumerates them read-only (`git ls-files -v -z` flags h/S and lowercase variants; compare the index oid to a no-filter hash of the working file) and ships them as Files entries (Restore reproduces the bytes and re-applies the flag), and Stamp includes their lstat so edits trigger capture. core.filemode=false repositories: the index mode is authoritative (the repo explicitly ignores the exec bit), documented, not a gap. (c) jj-workspace capture includes every file tracked by the workspace's @ (not only @-) even when .gitignore now matches it, matching Stamp. Tests for each against real git/jj; source read-only proof extended (fsmonitor hook + submodule-only filter sentinels never fire during Capture).

D15 (reposync; root round-trip review reviews/reposync-roundtrip.json at 76e7ece, 2026-09-26): (a) P1 unpublished-history LFS dependency detection must be independent of the CURRENT worktree attributes: for every blob introduced by commits in `HEAD ^TrunkTip`, decide LFS-ness by the attributes in effect in that commit (`git check-attr --source=<commit>` read-only) OR by strict LFS pointer-format parsing of small blobs (spec v1: `version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1` first line, `oid sha256:<64hex>`, `size <n>`, ≤ 1024 bytes), taking the union, so editing .gitattributes can never hide an object the unpublished HEAD requires; a required object absent from the local LFS store is MissingLFSError (never Complete/Ready). The staged-index and worktree LFS paths likewise use the attributes of the index/HEAD where relevant, never a later worktree edit alone. (b) P2 sparse config: read core.sparseCheckout / core.sparseCheckoutCone case-insensitively (git lowercases keys) plus the per-worktree config (extensions.worktreeConfig) so ordinary `git sparse-checkout` worktrees populate Snapshot.Sparse. (c) P2 restore honesty: the default Restore still expands to a full checkout (coordinator-chosen default: safest, no receiver repo config mutation), but when Snapshot.Sparse is set it must report Exact=false with a Difference naming "sparse checkout expanded to full" + the source patterns, and Restored.Sparse returns them; an explicit RestoreOptions.ApplySparse re-applies them in the new recovery worktree (`git sparse-checkout set [--cone|--no-cone]`, documented side effect: enables extensions.worktreeConfig on the receiver repo) and then Exact compares against the sparse expectation. cc-sync surfaces the expansion in pickup JSON/list and offers --apply-sparse. Tests: the reviewer's three reproductions with real git/git-lfs, each failing first.
  D15 SCOPE CLARIFICATION (root, 2026-09-26T21:25Z, binding): the D15 verification's cache-upgrade blocker concerns caches written by the unshipped intermediate commit 76e7ece. Do NOT build backward compatibility or migrations for unreleased intermediate cache/ledger formats: define a clean v1 cache/ledger format with an explicit identity/version and invalidate (discard + recapture) anything else. Keep real correctness: within the final version, an attribute change must reclassify affected paths (no stale cached LFS verdicts). The other D15 findings are concrete; the final reposync merge reconciles them with the overlapping fixes already on cc-sync/worktree-snapshot (3ea2d6b) instead of duplicating implementations, and removes any intermediate-cache compatibility code a lane added.
  D14 ADDENDUM (coordinator 2026-09-26T21:35Z, after delta review fix fd46c69): an intent-to-add path that was then deleted from disk (status `.D`, ita in index) is captured EXACTLY (option a): Capture records it in both IntentToAdd and Files(FileDeleted) — computing the intent-to-add set for unflagged paths too (the --ita-visible/--ita-invisible diff pair), and Restore creates an empty placeholder, runs `add -N`, then removes it, so the restored index/worktree match the source and Exact holds. Minimum git on every host: 2.44 (GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH; `sparse-checkout check-rules` needs 2.42) — Capture/Restore check `git version` once and fail with a typed error naming the requirement; document it in the reposync README and the cc-sync install preflight. Known remaining limit to report honestly (not a Complete=false trigger): files hidden by assume-unchanged/skip-worktree INSIDE a submodule make that submodule look clean (same as unflagged submodules' internal hidden files); the submodule itself is already an omission whenever git reports it dirty.

D16 (cc-sync catalog/consumer/service; root catalog review reviews/catalog.json @ 82c383d, coordinator judgment 2026-09-26T21:55Z, binding):
- Precise predicates, shared by ACK, retention, list/picker, and source-side assurance: Complete(cp) = code_state complete (not mixed/deferred) AND Completeness.Complete (every referenced session artifact archived) AND no omission; HeldReady(cp) = root closure complete in the local store AND the referenced code root's Verify verdict ready (for a mixed checkpoint: its older code root — no Mixed() bypass); PickupReady(cp) = Complete(cp) AND HeldReady(cp).
- ACK: the receiver ACKs a change's SourceRevision only when every UNEXPIRED checkpoint carried in it is HeldReady; otherwise Partial with the prior receipt (fixes F1). An incomplete or mixed checkpoint can be held (so newer session bytes are durable) but never counts as a complete recovery point.
- Retention (fixes F2): latest/hourly/daily tiers are computed over Complete checkpoints only; mixed/incomplete checkpoints newer than the worktree's latest Complete one are retained in addition (bounded: the newest per class) and can never evict a Complete checkpoint. Default pickup/list target = newest PickupReady.
- F3 expiry disposition: expired pending payload is never retained forever (7 d inactivity expiry + offline supersede forbid immortal pins). A checkpoint already expired (per the receiver's clock, ExpiresAt = source activity + 7 d, never renewed) when a change is applied is DISPOSED: not recorded, never ready, fence kept (no resurrection). A change whose unexpired checkpoints are all HeldReady is ACKed as processed (so the sender's pending clears) even if every checkpoint in it was disposed. That ACK is never a per-checkpoint durability claim: source-side assurance (cc-sync status/list/picker) shows checkpoint X as "durable on peer P" only if Complete(X) AND P.Acked ≥ X's catalog revision AND now < X.ExpiresAt; mixed/incomplete checkpoints show "held on P, not a complete recovery point"; expired ones show nothing. Document clock-skew honesty (assurance ends at ExpiresAt; peers' clocks may differ).
- Tests: F1 mixed without code verdict → Partial; mixed with verified older code → ACK, still not PickupReady; F2 incomplete-session newer checkpoint never evicts the last Complete one and is not the default pickup target; F3 pending partial checkpoint expires → replay of the same revision → processed ACK, catalog holds nothing live for it, source status shows no durability for it, no resurrection by a stale relay, source activity not renewed.
